142:     Parameters
143:     ----------
144:     freq_hz : np.ndarray
145:         Array of frequencies in Hz.
146:     base_frequency : float
147:         Base frequency for conversion.
148:         (Default value = 10.0)
149:     """
150:     freq_cent = np.zeros(freq_hz.shape[0])
151:     freq_nonz_ind = np.flatnonzero(freq_hz)
152:     normalized_frequency = np.abs(freq_hz[freq_nonz_ind]) / base_frequency
153:     freq_cent[freq_nonz_ind] = 1200.0 * np.log2(normalized_frequency)
154:     return freq_cent
155: 
156: 
157: def freq_to_voicing(frequencies, voicing=None):
158:     """Convert from an array of frequency values to frequency array +
159:     voice/unvoiced array
160: 
161:     Parameters
162:     ----------
163:     frequencies : np.ndarray
164:         Array of frequencies.  A frequency <= 0 indicates "unvoiced".
165: 
166:     voicing : np.ndarray
167:         Array of voicing values.
168:         (Default value = None)
169:         Default None, which means the voicing is inferred from `frequencies`:
170: 
171:            - frames with frequency <= 0.0 are considered "unvoiced"
172:            - frames with frequency > 0.0 are considered "voiced"
173: 
174:         If specified, `voicing` is used as the voicing array, but
175:         frequencies with value 0 are forced to have 0 voicing.
176: 
177:            - Voicing inferred by negative frequency values is ignored.
178: 
179:     Returns
180:     -------
181:     frequencies : np.ndarray
182:         Array of frequencies, all >= 0.
183:     voiced : np.ndarray
184:         Array of voicings between 0 and 1, same length as frequencies,
185:         which indicates voiced or unvoiced
186: 
187:     """
188:     if voicing is not None:
189:         voicing[frequencies == 0] = 0
190:     else:
191:         voicing = (frequencies > 0).astype(float)
192:     return np.abs(frequencies), voicing
193: 
194: 
195: def constant_hop_timebase(hop, end_time):
196:     """Generate a time series from 0 to ``end_time`` with times spaced ``hop`` apart
197: 
198:     Parameters
199:     ----------
200:     hop : float
201:         Spacing of samples in the time series
202:     end_time : float
203:         Time series will span ``[0, end_time]``
204: 
205:     Returns
206:     -------
207:     times : np.ndarray
208:         Generated timebase
209: 
210:     """
211:     # Compute new timebase.  Rounding/linspace is to avoid float problems.
212:     end_time = np.round(end_time, 10)
213:     times = np.linspace(
214:         0, hop * int(np.floor(end_time / hop)), int(np.floor(end_time / hop)) + 1
215:     )
216:     times = np.round(times, 10)
217:     return times
218: 
219: 
220: def resample_melody_series(times, frequencies, voicing, times_new, kind="linear"):
221:     """Resamples frequency and voicing time series to a new timescale. Maintains
222:     any zero ("unvoiced") values in frequencies.
223: 
224:     If ``times`` and ``times_new`` are equivalent, no resampling will be
225:     performed.
226: 
227:     Parameters
228:     ----------
229:     times : np.ndarray
230:         Times of each frequency value
231:     frequencies : np.ndarray
232:         Array of frequency values, >= 0
233:     voicing : np.ndarray
234:         Array which indicates voiced or unvoiced. This array may be binary
235:         or have continuous values between 0 and 1.
236:     times_new : np.ndarray
237:         Times to resample frequency and voicing sequences to
238:     kind : str
239:         kind parameter to pass to scipy.interpolate.interp1d.
240:         (Default value = 'linear')
241: 
242:     Returns
243:     -------
244:     frequencies_resampled : np.ndarray
245:         Frequency array resampled to new timebase
246:     voicing_resampled : np.ndarray
247:         Voicing array resampled to new timebase
248: 
249:     """
250:     # If the timebases are already the same, no need to interpolate
251:     if times.shape == times_new.shape and np.allclose(times, times_new):
252:         return frequencies, voicing
253: 
254:     # Warn when the delta between the original times is not constant,
255:     # unless times[0] == 0. and frequencies[0] == frequencies[1] (see logic at
256:     # the beginning of to_cent_voicing)
257:     if not (
258:         np.allclose(np.diff(times), np.diff(times).mean())
259:         or (
260:             np.allclose(np.diff(times[1:]), np.diff(times[1:]).mean())
261:             and frequencies[0] == frequencies[1]
262:         )
263:     ):
264:         warnings.warn(
265:             "Non-uniform timescale passed to resample_melody_series.  Pitch "
266:             "will be linearly interpolated, which will result in undesirable "
267:             "behavior if silences are indicated by missing values.  Silences "
268:             "should be indicated by nonpositive frequency values."
269:         )
270:     # Round to avoid floating point problems
271:     times = np.round(times, 10)
272:     times_new = np.round(times_new, 10)
273:     # Add in an additional sample if we'll be asking for a time too large
274:     if times_new.max() > times.max():
275:         times = np.append(times, times_new.max())
276:         frequencies = np.append(frequencies, 0)
277:         voicing = np.append(voicing, 0)
278:     # We need to fix zero transitions if interpolation is not zero or nearest
279:     if kind != "zero" and kind != "nearest":
280:         # Fill in zero values with the last reported frequency
281:         # to avoid erroneous values when resampling
282:         frequencies_held = np.array(frequencies)
283:         for n, frequency in enumerate(frequencies[1:]):
284:             if frequency == 0:
285:                 frequencies_held[n + 1] = frequencies_held[n]
286:         # Linearly interpolate frequencies
287:         frequencies_resampled = scipy.interpolate.interp1d(
288:             times, frequencies_held, kind
289:         )(times_new)
290:         # Retain zeros
291:         frequency_mask = scipy.interpolate.interp1d(times, frequencies, "zero")(
292:             times_new
293:         )
294:         frequencies_resampled *= frequency_mask != 0
295:     else:
296:         frequencies_resampled = scipy.interpolate.interp1d(times, frequencies, kind)(
297:             times_new
